title: Getting Around
tagline: Plan the routes for pupils, from the gate to class, the pool and the roof.
grownUp: This mission is about circulation, the way people move through a building, and about coding, which is giving clear steps in order.
In the coding games, ask the Architect to guess where the pupil will end up before pressing Go, then to fix one tile if the pupil gets stuck.
The Big Question has no right answer. A finish line gives runners a goal, and a loop lets them keep going. Both are good reasons.

steps.title: How people move around
steps.text: Circulation is how people move around a building, through doors, corridors, stairs and slides. Good circulation means nobody gets lost and nobody has to rush.
steps.ask: Where in your school would people hurry, and where would they stop to chat?

steps.title: Coding is giving clear steps
steps.text: Coding means giving very clear instructions, one step at a time. You will give your pupils picture tiles, such as Go to the pool, Swim and Again.
steps.ask: What would you tell your pupil to do first?

steps.title: Code your first pupil
steps.intro: Code a pupil from the gate to a classroom, then to the pool for a swim, and guess where they end up before you press Go.

steps.title: Which one only goes down?
steps.prompt: Which of these is a way that only goes down?
steps.reveal: A slide only goes down, so people use stairs or a climbing wall to get back up. Stairs and climbing walls can be used to go up as well as down.

steps.title: Run laps on the roof
steps.intro: Put the running track on the roof, add a way up, and code a pupil to run laps using the Again tile.

steps.title: Finish line or round and round?
steps.scenario: Should the roof track have a finish line, or go round and round for ever?

options.label: A finish line
options.detail: Runners have a goal, and they can say they finished the race.

options.label: Round and round for ever
options.detail: Nobody has to stop, so runners can keep going for as long as they like.

options.label: A finish line on a loop
options.detail: Runners can finish a race, and then keep going round if they want to.

steps.reveal: Architects think about what runners want, how much room there is and whether the track is easy for everyone to use. Some tracks are straight with a finish, and others are loops with no end.
steps.followUp: On your roof track, how would you know when you had finished a race?

steps.title: Walk your route at home
need: A grown-up to walk with you
steps: Walk slowly from the front door to your bedroom, and notice each door, corridor and stair.
Draw a map of the route as you walk, with a small dot at each doorway.
Walk it again, and mark with a star each place where people hurry or stop.
steps.why: Architects watch how people move before they decide where the doors and stairs should go.

debrief: Where would people hurry or gather in your school, and why?
